policy: Initial JavaScript, desktop route and Settings ceilings were lowered after measured P2 reductions. Other reviewed ceilings remain unchanged. The PDF viewer feature ceiling rose from 500000 to 510000 for the PDF.js 6 security upgrade (GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j); the chunk loads only when a PDF is opened. Locale-only ceilings include the existing reviewed 24-language supporter UI expansion, the shared key dictionary and every canonical translated value. Further increases require a performance review. The 4.1.0 performance review adds exactly 9002 canonical locale bytes (0.461%) and 611 bytes to the largest catalog for four caption/reload labels in all 24 locales. Dictionary plus English grows 368 bytes; dictionary plus the largest selected catalog grows 744 bytes, with unchanged loading requests. JavaScript, CSS, route, feature and literal ceilings are unchanged. Teragram local redesign performance review: CSS measures 146353 bytes (6353 bytes over the prior 140000 ceiling) and the desktop route measures 305030 bytes (3030 bytes over 302000). The new shell, responsive sign-in artwork and folder/type controls add no web fonts, external images or requests; virtualized rows and lazy media modules remain. Local ceilings are 148000 CSS and 307000 route bytes; all other ceilings remain unchanged. Teragram dashboard overhaul review: the three-column shell, masonry, allocation/settings controls and lightbox add local CSS (157975 bytes measured before final ad-style removal; ceiling 159000). 15 translated labels in 24 catalogs measure 1974959 total bytes and 140323 maximum catalog bytes; ceilings 1976000 and 140400. Modal focus and integrated actions move the lazy media chunk to 250144 bytes; ceiling 251000. Initial JS measures 500027, total JS 2412608, desktop route 291528 and Settings 122139, each below its existing ceiling. Inter is a single 876576-byte locally bundled variable TTF, with no runtime font request to a third party. Table rows remain virtualized; gallery mounting is progressive with viewport-driven thumbnails. No budget check is removed. Teragram Photos/Notion polish review: final CSS is 167543 bytes, including the single immersive HUD, neutral shell, sidebar storage popover, accent controls and thumbnail states; reviewed ceiling 169000. Ten new labels in 24 catalogs bring locale totals to 1982485 bytes and maximum catalog to 140802; reviewed ceilings 1984000 and 141000. Initial JS is 494738 bytes, total JS 2386165, desktop route 301969, Settings 116264 and media 226436, all within unchanged JavaScript ceilings. Preset/editor UI removal reduces initial and media code; no new dependency or external asset request is added. All checks remain enabled. Teragram floating-preview polish review: CSS measures 172371 bytes for glass backdrop/window transitions, explicit fullscreen, Settings control alignment and header layout. Reviewed CSS ceiling 174000; all JS and locale ceilings remain unchanged. Initial JS remains 494738 bytes, desktop route 305003 (below 307000), Settings 115932 and media 226514. No dependency or external request was introduced. Final follow-up measurements: CSS 172419 bytes, total JS 2389243 and desktop route 305197; reviewed ceilings remain unchanged from this polish review. Teragram Material 3 shell review: measured CSS 184682 bytes, desktop route 313188 bytes, initial JS 494880 bytes, total JS 2397289 bytes, locale total 1988396 and largest catalog 141373. The stationary/recessed shell, persisted floating/rail navigation, keyboard/focus handling, tooltips and folder menus add no dependencies, third-party requests or fonts. Table virtualization uses the single workspace scroller; media stays lazy. Reviewed ceilings: CSS 185500, desktop route 315000, locale total 1990000, largest catalog 142000. Other ceilings and all checks remain unchanged.
notes: Teragram macOS functional polish review: measured total CSS 187127 bytes before the final bounded-track rule. The document viewer adds local monospace, line numbers and code token styling; old floating-sidebar styles were removed. Reviewed CSS ceiling 188000 bytes. The new text viewer is lazy, uses the existing virtualizer and adds no dependencies, remote assets or fonts. All JavaScript, locale and feature ceilings remain unchanged. Teragram v1.0 review: measured CSS 196169 bytes before final accessibility/motion rules; ceiling 198000. Locale totals are 2001166 bytes and largest catalog 142316, reflecting 13 translated movie-control labels and folder expansion labels across 24 catalogs; ceilings 2003000 and 142500. Desktop route measures 317787 bytes before the Settings shortcut handler; ceiling 319000. Initial JS 495006, total JS 2416734, Settings 114055 and media 228661 remain within unchanged ceilings. Window-only gallery breakpoints eliminate sidebar-frame ResizeObserver updates; existing virtualization, lazy movie/PDF modules, and bounded thumbnail loading remain. No dependency, font, or third-party runtime request was added. CSS animations and FLIP respect reduced motion. Full view accessibility and stable-node/column journeys remain enabled. Final Teragram measurements: CSS 197543, initial JS 495295, desktop route 317977 and total JS 2417518 bytes; all reviewed ceilings pass. Teragram refinement review: the import dialog is lazy and bounded to 100 rendered rows initially, with three visible-row avatar/detail workers. Initial JS falls to about 492281 bytes after remote-crash consent/queue removal; the desktop route measures 320637 bytes including local folder refresh and import/detach controls (ceiling 322000). CSS 201069 bytes (ceiling 202000) adds corrected toolbar geometry, trailing tree actions and the channel picker. Thirteen translated labels and the requested About copy bring locale data to 2019160 bytes, largest catalog 143593 (ceilings 2021000 and 143800). The import feature has its own 10000-byte lazy-chunk budget. No new dependency, remote font, analytics request, or telemetry transport is introduced. Original-preview memory accounting and bounded adjacent prefetch remain in place.
